candidate.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — transmission-based precautions and infection control
candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — C. difficile contact precautions
candidate.educational_objective: Apply current CDC duration guidance for C. difficile contact precautions and question premature discontinuation.

options.A: Clarify the plan because CDC recommends maintaining contact precautions for at least 48 hours after diarrhea resolves, and facilities may continue them longer through hospitalization
options.B: Discontinue precautions immediately because C. difficile precautions end with the first formed stool
options.C: Continue precautions for life because a prior C. difficile infection permanently requires isolation
options.D: Use contact precautions only during toileting because transmission does not occur from the client's environment

candidate.rationale: CDC acute-care guidance updated in May 2026 recommends maintaining contact precautions for confirmed C. difficile infection for at least 48 hours after diarrhea has resolved, with longer continuation up to the duration of hospitalization in some settings. C. difficile spores can contaminate the environment, so precautions are not limited to toileting encounters.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Confirmed CDI requires contact precautions for at least 48 hours after diarrhea resolves, potentially longer through hospitalization.
candidate.source_document_title: Clinical Guidance for C. diff Infection Prevention in Acute Care Facilities
candidate.source_locator: Isolate and initiate contact precautions — confirmed CDI: maintain contact precautions for at least 48 hours after diarrhea has resolved, or longer up to duration of hospitalization
candidate.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
candidate.stem: A hospitalized client with confirmed C. difficile infection has had no diarrhea since this morning. A plan is entered to discontinue contact precautions immediately. Which action should the nurse take?
